name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,791

entries.clue: Astronaut best among stars when rotated (8)

indicatorNotes.among: 'among' places one thing in the middle of others, so CAP sits inside NAMES
indicatorNotes.when rotated: something rotated half a turn faces the other way, so the letters run backwards

annotation.surface: An astronaut outshines the stars as the spacecraft spins.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like an adjective praising the astronaut, but it is the verb: to cap or top something. NAME(CAP)S, turned round, reads as the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name someone who travels beyond the atmosphere, the shorter one being the older, informal term.

entries.clue: One shooting bird on river (6)

blocks.note: the snipe is a wading bird

annotation.surface: A hunter takes aim at a bird perched by the river.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'One shooting bird' a single phrase about hunting; the split comes after 'One shooting'. In a down clue, 'on' puts SNIPE above R.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the answer is a marksman who fires from cover, literally one who is shooting.

entries.clue: Almighty muddle in poem not finally relevant (10)

indicatorNotes.muddle: a muddle is a confused jumble, so the letters are to be jumbled
indicatorNotes.finally: 'finally' points to what comes last, so only the last letter of 'relevant' is used

annotation.surface: A critic grumbles that some grand muddle in a poem is beside the point.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not finally relevant' reads as 'irrelevant in the end', but 'not' is fodder in its own right and 'finally' takes only the T.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'the Almighty' is God, and the answer describes unlimited power, God's defining attribute.

entries.clue: One seen on beach, footballer carrying two books (6)

indicatorNotes.carrying: someone carrying a load holds it within their arms, so PELE holds BB inside

annotation.surface: A footballer on the beach with a couple of paperbacks under his arm.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface puts a person on the beach; the definition means a thing, one of the many pebbles there. PE(BB)LE.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a small smooth stone is exactly the kind of thing you see on a shingle beach.

entries.clue: Quick way round two problems with electricity (5,3)

blocks.note: a short (circuit) is one electrical fault
a power cut is the other

annotation.surface: An electrician finds a fast fix around two faults in the wiring.
annotation.walkthrough: One phrase supplies both halves: a short circuit and a power cut are the 'two problems with electricity'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a quicker route than the usual one, taken literally or figuratively to save time.

entries.clue: Surrounded by morning papers (4)

annotation.surface: Someone buried in the morning newspapers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Papers' is not the newspapers the surface suggests but identity papers, ID.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the preposition: in the middle of things, with them all around.

entries.clue: Old Bob manipulated leaving sinister controller (8)

indicatorNotes.manipulated: to manipulate is to handle and rearrange, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a bob was a shilling, abbreviated s. in old British money

annotation.surface: Old Bob was manipulated into leaving by a sinister figure pulling his strings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old Bob' looks like a man's name; it is pre-1971 British money, where a bob was a shilling, written s. 'Leaving' looks like a verb of departure but is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: An eponym: the hypnotist in George du Maurier's novel Trilby, whose name now means anyone who controls another malignly.

entries.clue: Contractor told to purchase mushrooms (6)

indicatorNotes.told: something told is spoken aloud, so the answer is heard rather than spelt

annotation.surface: A builder is told to go and buy some mushrooms.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Contractor' suggests a builder; here it is a muscle, which works by contracting.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic sense: a muscle works by contracting, so it can playfully be called a contractor.

entries.clue: Boozer with French name, writer hot in Asian city (5,4)

annotation.surface: A drinker with a French name and a writer swelter in an Asian city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' is British slang for a pub, and PH is the map abbreviation for public house.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the capital of Cambodia, on the Mekong.

entries.clue: Fruity ice lolly from MI5 and 6? (5)

blocks.note: MI kept, 5 as the Roman numeral V

annotation.surface: A fruity ice lolly apparently issued by the British secret services.
annotation.walkthrough: MI5 and MI6 are the British security and intelligence services; write the numbers as Roman numerals. A Mivvi is a British ice lolly with an ice-cream core.
annotation.definitionFit: A brand name: a British lolly with a fruit-ice shell round an ice-cream core, sold since the 1930s.

entries.clue: Month cut short on cold island (5)

indicatorNotes.cut short: a thing cut short loses its end, so the month drops its last letter

annotation.surface: A chilly month cut short on an island holiday.
annotation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'A on B' puts A after B, so APRI follows C.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a rocky island in the Bay of Naples, famous for the Blue Grotto.

entries.clue: Prohibit canned nuts in country event (4,5)

indicatorNotes.nuts: nuts means crazy, and crazy letters do not stay in order

annotation.surface: A ban on tinned nuts at a country show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Canned nuts' reads as tinned food, but 'nuts' is the anagram indicator acting on 'canned'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a social evening of folk or square dancing, originally held in a barn.

entries.clue: Kit the writer placed far down, loading horse (7)

indicatorNotes.loading: loading a horse puts cargo on board, so LOW goes inside MARE

blocks.note: a mare is a female horse

annotation.surface: A writer's kit is stowed deep in the hold while a horse is loaded.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kit' looks like gear to be stowed; it is the nickname of the Elizabethan playwright Christopher Marlowe. MAR(LOW)E.
annotation.definitionFit: A nickname: Christopher Marlowe, the Elizabethan playwright of Doctor Faustus, was known as Kit.

entries.clue: Body in vehicle about to join ship (7)

annotation.surface: A body is found in a car on its way to board a ship.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a crime report; 'in' is only the link between definition and wordplay, not a container instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the dead body of an animal, and loosely of a person.

entries.clue: Scarlet woman's cabal causing diversion (3,7)

blocks.note: a ring is a secret group, a cabal

annotation.surface: A scarlet woman's secret circle stirs up a distraction.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scarlet woman' is a set phrase for an immoral woman, so the clue seems to be about her; the words work separately. A cabal is a secret faction.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: a smoked fish supposedly dragged across a trail to throw hounds off the scent, hence any distraction.

entries.clue: Trap quickly springs back — end of mouse (5)

indicatorNotes.springs back: something that springs back returns the way it came, so the word runs backwards
indicatorNotes.end of: the end of a word is its last letter

annotation.surface: A mousetrap snaps shut — curtains for the mouse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Springs back' is exactly what a sprung trap does, which disguises it as a reversal instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a loop of rope that tightens when pulled, used as a snare.

entries.clue: Infatuated old queen entertaining second journalist (8)

indicatorNotes.entertaining: a host entertaining a guest has them inside the house, so BESS contains S

annotation.surface: An ageing queen, besotted, plays host to a junior reporter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Old queen' feels like one unit, but 'old' gives O on its own and the queen is Elizabeth I's nickname Bess, holding S: O + B(S)ESS + ED.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone whose thoughts are wholly taken up by one person or thing.

entries.clue: Obstruction encountered in Little Thurrock (3)

indicatorNotes.encountered in: what is encountered in a phrase is met inside it, so the answer lies within the words

annotation.surface: A roadblock met with in Little Thurrock, a village in Essex.
annotation.walkthrough: The old sense of let survives in the legal phrase 'without let or hindrance' and in tennis, where a let is a serve obstructed by the net.
annotation.definitionFit: An old sense kept in law and tennis: 'without let or hindrance', and a serve obstructed by the net.

entries.clue: Whence one cross, in traditional tales, drops from sky (8)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition is a riddle for a place: the region the Cross of Lorraine is named after.

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' puts one thing inside another, so RAIN goes within LORE

annotation.surface: A cross falls out of the sky, as in the old folk tales.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a verb or a mood; it is the double-barred Cross of Lorraine, emblem of the Free French. LOR(RAIN)E.
annotation.definitionFit: A riddle-style definition: the double-barred cross is named after the French region, so that is where one cross comes from.

entries.clue: Democrat at fault reveals tendency (5)

blocks.note: a rift is a fault, as in the rock

annotation.surface: A Democrat caught in the wrong shows which way he leans.
annotation.walkthrough: 'At fault' reads as 'to blame', but 'fault' is the geological kind, a rift.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the general direction or gist of something, as in 'I get your drift'.

entries.clue: Unlucky for being abandoned? That's harsh! (8)

indicatorNotes.being abandoned: something abandoned is left behind, so FOR drops out of the longer word

annotation.surface: Someone moans that being dumped is unlucky, and harsh too.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unlucky for' sounds like the start of 'unlucky for some'. Instead, find a long word for unlucky that begins with FOR and let it go.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: lacking melody, so grating on the ear.

entries.clue: Sex position ordinary with Romeo's guest (7)

blocks.note: sex is Latin for six, VI in Roman numerals
to sit is to take a position
O = ordinary, from the old O level exams
Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A saucy account of Romeo's bedroom antics with his guest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sex position' is the obvious reading and a deliberate tease: 'sex' is Latin six. The 's after Romeo stands for 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who comes to stay or call.

entries.clue: Entering Shetland bay German alas makes return journey (6)

indicatorNotes.Entering: one thing entering another goes inside it, so the reversed piece goes into VOE
indicatorNotes.return: to return is to go back the way you came, so G + AY runs backwards

blocks.note: a voe is an inlet in Shetland or Orkney
ay = an old cry of woe, as in 'ay me'

annotation.surface: A German laments as he sails into a Shetland bay and heads home again.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Return journey' looks like the definition; 'return' is the reversal indicator and 'journey' alone defines. VO(YAG)E.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, usually for a long trip by sea or through space.

entries.clue: Prepare without finishing and study in China (7)

indicatorNotes.without finishing: a word without its finish lacks its final letter, so DRESS loses an S

blocks.note: to dress (a salad, a chicken) = to prepare; DRESS minus its last S
a den is a study, a private room

annotation.surface: Someone prepares for study in China but never finishes.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital C of 'China' sends you to the country; it is porcelain, and Dresden china is the famous Meissen ware.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword sense of 'China' as porcelain: fine Meissen ware, made near the Saxon city it is named after.

entries.clue: Detective Sergeant arresting little British idiots (6)

indicatorNotes.arresting: police arresting someone take them into custody, so DS holds WEE B inside

annotation.surface: A detective sergeant rounds up some small-time British fools.
annotation.walkthrough: D(WEE B)S: the detective's initials split around the captured pair.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in slang: boring, socially inept people, an American import.

entries.clue: Audacious favourite losing heart (6)

indicatorNotes.losing heart: the heart of a word is its middle, so the central letter goes

blocks.note: the middle letter of DARLING goes

annotation.surface: A bold favourite loses their nerve.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Losing heart' reads as losing courage, the opposite of audacious; here it removes the middle letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: bold and willing to take risks.

entries.clue: Hands-free connection with this number? (3,2,4,2,7)

blocks.note: a hand is a bunch of bananas, so free of hands = no bananas

annotation.surface: A question about hands-free phone connections and a phone number.
annotation.walkthrough: The telephone picture is the disguise: a hand of bananas is a bunch, and 'number' is a song, the 1920s hit 'Yes! We Have No Bananas'.
annotation.definitionFit: The song title declares a total absence of bananas, and a hand is a bunch of them, so the singer is hands-free.

entries.clue: Sicilian eminence wants petunia in prime locations (4)

indicatorNotes.in prime locations: prime here is the number sense, so read the letters at positions 2, 3, 5 and 7

annotation.surface: A Sicilian dignitary wants petunias in the best spots.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prime locations' sounds like estate-agent talk; it means prime-numbered positions, an unusual but exact instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an eminence is a high point of land, and the volcano is Sicily's highest.

entries.clue: King meets important Russian banker in country (5)

blocks.note: a banker is a river, having banks; the Ural is a major Russian river

annotation.surface: A king has a meeting with a powerful Russian financier.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Banker' suggests money; in crosswords it is a river, the thing with banks.
annotation.definitionFit: The adjective 'country' as in country life: belonging to the countryside rather than the town.

entries.clue: Place for putting vegetable — Chartreuse? (5)

blocks.note: golf: the closely mown area where you putt
leafy vegetables go by a colour word, as in 'eat up your ...s'
a pale yellowish shade, named after the liqueur

annotation.surface: Where should the vegetables go — in the Chartreuse bottle?
annotation.walkthrough: Three meanings, not two: golf's putting green, greens as vegetables, and chartreuse the colour, named after the green liqueur.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the closely mown area round a golf hole, and the colour of which chartreuse is a yellowish shade.

entries.clue: See 24
